newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Komi republic cannot issue Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Komi republic cannot issue Eurobonds.

text.p: Russia's northern Komi republic does not have the right to issue a Eurobond as the territory receives monetary assistance from the federal government, the head of the Finance Ministry's securities department said on Wednesday.
When asked whether Komi republic could issue a Eurobond, Bella Zlatkis answered: "No."
She told a news conference that according to Russian legislation only regions and territories which could manage without help from the federal budget had the right to issue Eurobonds.
On Tuesday senior Komi officials said in London that the republic planned to issue a $200 million five-year Eurobond by the end of the year.
Zlatkis said only eight territories had the right to issue Eurobonds according to the 1997 budget, adding the number of such territories in 1998 was likely to be less.
She said Irkutsk region, Tatar republic, Mary El republic and Sverdlovsk region had announced plans to issue Eurobonds.
The City of Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod region are also planning Eurobond issues.
Vladimir Tarachyov, a member of the State Duma lower house of parliament's budget committee, told the news conference that Russian territories were planning the following Eurobonds:
Nizhny Novgorod region $100 million
Sverdlovsk region $20 million
Chelyabinsk region $100 million
Irkutsk region $100 million
St Petersburg $300 million
Tatar republic $200 million
Moscow $400 million
Moscow region $400 million
Tarachyov works on laws on municipal borrowing on the committee.
Zlatkis said the Finance Ministry may register the St Petersburg Eurobond prospectus tonight and Nizhny Novgorod region planned to present its prospectus soon.
She said the ministry had registered the City of Moscow's prospectus several days ago with a planned volume of $400-500 million.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
